title: Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Restoration of Honor of and Compensation to Persons Related to Democratization Movements
title_original: 민주화운동관련자 명예회복 및 보상 등에 관한 법률 시행령
full_text:
Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Restoration of Honor of and Compensation to Persons Related to Democratization Movements

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Act on the Restoration of Honor of and Compensation to Persons Related to Democratization Movements and matters necessary for its enforcement. <Amended on April 15, 2005>

Article 2 (Definitions)
"Resistance" under subparagraph 1 of Article 2 of the Act on the Restoration of Honor of and Compensation to Persons Related to Democratization Movements (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") includes not only direct resistance to State power but also cases in which, by resisting violence or other acts committed by employers or other persons in the course of State power's suppression of democratization movements arising in various sectors of society, such as schools, the press, and labor, a person ultimately resisted the rule of State power: Provided, That cases of resistance to violence or other acts of employers, etc. unrelated to State power shall be excluded. <Amended on April 15, 2005>

Article 3 (Diseases Related to Democratization Movements)
"Diseases prescribed by Presidential Decree" in subparagraph 2 (c) of Article 2 of the Act means diseases that the Disability Grade Determination Subcommittee under Article 7 (1) recognizes as qualifying for compensation and medical support payments.

Article 4 (Composition and Operation of the Deliberation Committee on the Restoration of Honor of and Compensation to Persons Related to Democratization Movements)
(1) Members of the Deliberation Committee on the Restoration of Honor of and Compensation to Persons Related to Democratization Movements under Article 4 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Committee") shall be appointed from among persons with extensive experience in or knowledge of democratization movements.
(2) The chairperson of the Committee shall convene and preside over its meetings.
(3) Where the chairperson is unable to perform his or her duties due to an unavoidable reason, a member designated in advance by the chairperson shall act on his or her behalf.
(4) A meeting of the Committee shall commence with a majority of all incumbent members present, and resolutions shall be adopted with the consent of a majority of the members present.

Article 5 (Functions of the Committee)
(1) "Other matters related to restoration of honor, compensation, etc. prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 4 (2) 7 of the Act means the following matters:
1. Deleted. <April 15, 2005>
2. Matters concerning methods of raising donations and plans for their use, etc. under Article 22 of the Act;
3. Matters concerning determination of the types of commemorative projects related to democratization movements, etc. under Article 23 of the Act;
4. Other major matters related to restoration of honor, compensation, etc.
(2) The Committee shall recommend to the President the results of its deliberations and decisions concerning specific measures for restoring honor under Article 4 (2) 4 of the Act, announce the results of the measures taken in the Official Gazette, and also announce them in two or more daily newspapers, on a website, through broadcasting, or by similar means. <Amended on November 24, 2020>

Article 5-2 (Issuance of Certificates to Persons Related to Democratization Movements)
The certificate for persons related to democratization movements prescribed in Article 5-2 of the Act shall be in Attached Form 11.

Article 5-3 (Procedures for Recommending Reinstatement)
(1) Where the Committee recommends reinstatement to an employer pursuant to Article 5-4 of the Act, the recommendation shall include a statement that the person concerned shall not suffer any disadvantage in personnel matters, such as salary steps, remuneration, promotion, career record, or pension, due to the dismissal.
(2) Where no employer under paragraph (1) exists, the Committee may recommend to the President that the Government or a government-affiliated institution employ the person concerned or arrange employment for that person.

Article 5-4 (Examples of Discriminatory Treatment and Disadvantageous Acts)
"Discriminatory treatment and disadvantages" in Article 5-6 of the Act means restrictions on employment, refusal to issue a passport, discriminatory treatment while serving a sentence, disadvantages in personnel matters, etc.

Article 5-5 (Standing Investigative Commissioner)
(1) The standing investigative commissioner under Article 5 (4) of the Act shall be appointed by the President upon the recommendation of the chairperson from among persons falling under the following subparagraphs and shall be a public official in general service belonging to the Senior Executive Service: <Amended on February 29, 2012; November 20, 2013>
1. A person who has served as a judge, prosecutor, military judicial officer, or attorney-at-law for at least five years;
2. A person who has served as an assistant professor or in a higher position at an accredited university for at least eight years;
3. A person who holds or has held a position as a public official of Grade III or higher or as a public official belonging to the Senior Executive Service and who has served as a public official for at least five years;
4. A person who has at least 10 years of research activity or experience concerning democratization movements.
(2) The term of office of the standing investigative commissioner shall be two years and may be renewed once.
(3) Under the direction of the chairperson, the standing investigative commissioner shall assist with the following matters and may attend and speak at meetings of the Committee:
1. Analysis, organization, and supplementation of agenda items to be submitted to the Committee;
2. Research and examination of other necessary matters.

Article 5-6 (Ex Officio Reconsideration)
(1) Matters subject to ex officio reconsideration under Article 5-7 of the Act shall be gathered and deliberated on in the final month of each half-year: Provided, That this shall not apply to an agenda item for which the Committee finds grounds for urgent ex officio reconsideration.
(2) The methods and procedures for ex officio reconsideration shall follow the Committee's general deliberation procedures.

Article 6 (Executive Secretary of the Committee)
(1) The Committee shall have one executive secretary to handle its affairs.
(2) The executive secretary shall be designated by the Minister of the Interior and Safety from among public officials belonging to the Senior Executive Service. <Amended on August 4, 2026>
(3) The executive secretary shall handle the affairs of the Committee under the direction of the chairperson and may attend and speak at meetings of the Committee.

Article 7 (Composition of Subcommittees)
(1) The Committee shall have the following subcommittees: <Amended on April 15, 2005>
1. A Subcommittee for Examining the Status of Related Persons and Surviving Family Members, which handles the affairs under Article 4 (2) 1 of the Act;
2. A Disability Grade Determination Subcommittee, which handles the affairs under Article 4 (2) 2 of the Act;
3. A Subcommittee for Promoting the Restoration of Honor, which handles the affairs under Article 4 (2) 4 of the Act;
4. A Subcommittee for Reviewing Livelihood Support Payments, which selects persons eligible for livelihood support payments under Article 9 of the Act and performs related duties;
5. A Subcommittee for Supporting National Commemorative Projects and Memorial Projects, which handles the affairs under Articles 23 and 24 of the Act.
(2) Each subcommittee under subparagraphs 1 and 3 through 5 shall be composed of not more than 10 members appointed or commissioned by the chairperson from among persons with extensive experience in or knowledge of democratization movements and shall include three persons recommended by memorial organizations under Article 24 (1) of the Act. <Amended on April 15, 2005>
(3) The Disability Grade Determination Subcommittee under subparagraph 2 shall be composed of not more than 15 members qualified as medical specialists under Article 55 of the Medical Service Act and shall include five persons recommended by memorial organizations under Article 24 (1) of the Act. <Newly Inserted on April 15, 2005>
(4) The chairperson of each subcommittee under the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) shall be elected by and from among the members of that subcommittee. <Newly Inserted on April 15, 2005>
(5) The term of office of a member of a subcommittee under the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) shall be two years and may be renewed. <Newly Inserted on April 15, 2005>
(6) Matters necessary for the operation of subcommittees shall be determined by the chairperson following a resolution of the Committee.

Article 8 (Allowances)
(1) Allowances and travel expenses may be paid, within budgetary limits, to members attending meetings of the Committee and its subcommittees: Provided, That this shall not apply where a member who is a public official attends a meeting in direct connection with the affairs under his or her jurisdiction. <Amended on April 15, 2005>
(2) Travel expenses and actual expenses may be paid, within budgetary limits, to witnesses or persons giving statements who appear before the Committee, etc. pursuant to Article 20 of the Act.

Article 9 (Application of Average Wages)
(1) Where no materials proving the average wages under Article 7 (3) of the Act are available, monthly pay or daily labor wages according to nationwide statistics by sex and occupation compiled by a wage survey institution that regularly publishes wage statistics at least once each year shall be used as average wages, etc.: Provided, That where no nationwide statistics are available, daily labor wages according to local statistics for the Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan City, or Do (hereinafter referred to as a "City/Do") having jurisdiction over the person's address at the relevant time shall be used.
(2) The average wages under paragraph (1) shall first be based on the statistics in the Survey Report on Wage Structure of the Ministry of Employment and Labor; where no basic wage structure statistics are available, the construction wage rate statistics of the National Data Agency shall be used; and where no construction wage rate statistics are available either, monthly pay or daily labor wages of ordinary laborers by sex surveyed using a credible method shall be used: Provided, That the minimum wage amount to be applied shall be the average wage for men or women, as applicable, in 1972 according to the statistics in the Survey Report on Actual Wages by Occupation of the Ministry of Employment and Labor. <Amended on July 12, 2010; January 5, 2021; October 1, 2025>

Article 10 (Deduction of Living Expenses)
In calculating compensation for surviving family members pursuant to Article 7 (4) of the Act, living expenses shall be deducted from monthly pay, monthly net earnings, or average wages in accordance with Attached Table 1. <Amended on October 31, 2007>

Article 11 (Employable Periods, Physical Disability Grades, and Rates of Loss of Working Capacity)
(1) Employable periods under Article 7 (5) of the Act shall be as specified in Attached Table 2, and physical disability grades and rates of loss of working capacity shall be as specified in Attached Table 3.
(2) Where there are two bodily regions with physical disabilities, the grade for each region shall first be determined under Attached Table 3, and a combined assessment grade shall then be determined under Attached Table 4.
(3) Where there are three or more bodily regions with physical disabilities, a combined assessment grade under Attached Table 4 shall first be determined for the two regions with the most severe disabilities; that combined assessment grade and the most severe disability among the remaining regions shall then be assessed together again under Attached Table 4 to determine the grade.
(4) Where there are at least three bodily regions whose most severe disabilities fall under physical disability Grade 14 in Attached Table 3, physical disability Grade 13 in Attached Table 3 shall apply.
(5) Where a person who has been notified by the Committee to undergo an examination at a designated hospital, etc. for determination of a disability grade fails to undergo such examination within one year from the date of notification, the Committee may classify that person as ungraded. In such cases, the Committee shall, three months before classifying that person as ungraded, notify the person of the possibility of being classified as ungraded and provide a final opportunity to undergo an examination.

Article 11-2 (Payment of Adjusted Compensation)
(1) Payment of adjusted compensation under Article 7-2 of the Act shall be limited to cases where the compensation under Article 7 (1) 1 or 2 (b) of the Act is less than the compensation to be paid on an adjusted basis.
(2) The compensation to be paid on an adjusted basis under paragraph (1) shall be the amount calculated by multiplying the standard wage in effect at the time the Committee decides on the adjusted payment (meaning the monthly equivalent of the minimum wage publicly announced pursuant to Article 10 (1) of the Minimum Wage Act) by the Hoffmann coefficient prescribed in attached Table 2 and the rate of loss of working capacity prescribed in attached Table 3. Provided, That the statutory interest rate under Article 7 (1) of the Act and the deduction of living expenses under Article 7 (4) of the Act shall not apply. <Amended on October 31, 2007>

Article 12 (Medical Support Payments)
Medical support payments under Article 8 (1) and (3) of the Act, including future treatment expenses, nursing care expenses, expenses for purchasing assistive devices, and treatment expenses already paid, shall be the amounts calculated by the following methods: <Amended on April 15, 2005; October 31, 2007; January 5, 2021; October 1, 2025>
1. Future treatment expenses shall be the amount calculated on the basis of an estimate of treatment expenses issued by a national general hospital, a hospital affiliated with a medical college (excluding branch hospitals), or a hospital designated by the Committee (hereinafter referred to as "designated hospitals, etc."). Provided, That where a designated hospital, etc. recognizes the need for future treatment expenses but is unable to estimate them, the amount shall be determined by the Committee, taking into consideration the opinion of the Disability Grade Determination Subcommittee and future treatment expenses in similar cases.
2. Nursing care expenses shall, where it is recognized on the basis of a medical certificate issued by a designated hospital, etc. that a person related to democratization movements has a physical disability even after full recovery and has difficulty engaging in activities without the care of another person, be the amount calculated by multiplying the amount determined by the Committee, taking into account the opinion of the Disability Grade Determination Subcommittee, within the range of the nursing allowance under Article 26 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State, by the average remaining life expectancy as of the date the Act enters into force, as periodically published by the National Data Agency.
3. Expenses for purchasing assistive devices shall, where the need to wear an assistive device is recognized on the basis of a medical certificate issued by a designated hospital, etc., be the amount calculated by multiplying the number of purchases deemed necessary during the average remaining life expectancy, according to the useful life of the assistive device, by the market purchase price.
4. Treatment expenses already paid by the injured person personally (hereinafter referred to as "previously paid treatment expenses") shall be determined by the Committee, taking into account the amounts calculated by the Disability Grade Determination Subcommittee as specified in the following items and previously paid treatment expenses in similar cases, by applying only the direct treatment expenses incurred in treating the relevant injury from the date of injury through the date of application for payment of previously paid treatment expenses; the calculation of future treatment expenses shall apply from the day following the date of application for payment of previously paid treatment expenses. Provided, That, for a person for whom a decision to pay compensation was made before the application for previously paid treatment expenses, the amount shall be determined by applying the period from the date of injury through the day preceding the date of the decision to pay compensation, and the calculation of future treatment expenses shall apply from the date of the decision to pay compensation.
(a) Where the applicant submits bills or receipts concerning previously paid treatment expenses issued by the relevant medical care institution, the amount shall be calculated, within the limit of 90 million won, by adding interest at the statutory interest rate for the period from the date the treatment expenses were paid through the date of application for previously paid treatment expenses to the amount recognized upon assessing the relationship between the out-of-pocket amounts on those bills or receipts and the injuries already recognized; where this amount is less than the amount calculated by the method in item (b), the amount under item (b) shall apply. Provided, That the amount shall not be calculated by adding together any part or the whole of the amounts calculated under items (a) and (b).
(b) Where bills or receipts concerning previously paid treatment expenses cannot be submitted, the amount shall be calculated by applying the criteria in attached Table 5, taking into account the injuries already recognized.

Article 12-2 (Livelihood Support Payments)
(1) Among persons eligible for livelihood support payments under Article 9 (1) of the Act, a person who was detained for at least 30 days shall be paid an amount calculated by multiplying the number of days of the relevant detention by the standard median income, but the amount shall not exceed 50 million won. In such cases, the standard median income to be applied shall be the amount calculated by dividing by 30 days an amount equivalent to 40 percent of the standard median income under Article 2, subparagraph 11 of the National Basic Living Security Act (meaning the standard median income for a four-person household) for the year in which the decision to make the livelihood support payment is made. <Amended on November 30, 2015>
(2) Among persons eligible for livelihood support payments under Article 9 (1) of the Act, a dismissed person with a length of service of at least one year shall be paid livelihood support payments according to the criteria in attached Table 6 for the period of dismissal recognized by the Committee; the period of dismissal and the mandatory retirement age shall be calculated according to the following criteria: <Newly inserted on October 31, 2007>
1. The period of dismissal shall run from the date of dismissal from the relevant workplace through the day preceding mandatory retirement or the day preceding reinstatement or special appointment, and, for persons who have not reached the mandatory retirement age, the end date of the period of dismissal shall be no later than November 26, 2007. Provided, That a period of service of at least one year in the same or a similar type of occupation may be excluded from the period of dismissal, and the specific criteria for the same or similar types of occupation shall be prescribed by the Committee.
2. The mandatory retirement age shall be 55 years, but an exception may be made where documentary evidence of the mandatory retirement age at the relevant workplace is submitted.
(3) Notwithstanding paragraphs (1) and (2), livelihood support payments shall not be made in any of the following cases: <Amended on June 12, 2006; October 23, 2007; October 31, 2007; November 1, 2011; November 20, 2013; May 28, 2014; October 1, 2025>
1. A person whose annual household income for the year preceding the application for livelihood support payments exceeds the annual aggregate of average monthly household expenditure per household, by the number of household members, for urban worker households in the preceding year's household survey, according to designated statistics publicly announced by the head of the National Data Agency pursuant to Article 22 of the Enforcement Decree of the Statistics Act;
2. A person who, as of the date this Decree enters into force, has served for at least one year in any of the following positions:
(a) Among public officials in career service under Article 2 of the State Public Officials Act and Article 2 of the Local Public Officials Act, public officials in general service of Grade 5 or higher (including public officials in general service belonging to the Senior Civil Service), and public officials in specific service who receive treatment equivalent to an intended appointment grade of Grade 5 or higher (including public officials in general service belonging to the Senior Civil Service) in the table of experience criteria by intended grade for career competitive recruitment, etc. under Article 27 (3) of the Decree on Examinations for Appointment of Public Officials;
(b) Among public officials in special career service under Article 2 of the State Public Officials Act and Article 2 of the Local Public Officials Act, public officials in political service and public officials in extraordinary service equivalent to Grade 5 or higher (including public officials in extraordinary service belonging to the Senior Civil Service); among fixed-term public officials under Article 2 of the State Public Officials Act and Article 35 of the Public Officials Remuneration Regulations, general fixed-term public officials at annual salary grade 5 or higher and specialized fixed-term public officials at Grade B or higher; and among local fixed-term public officials under Article 2 of the Local Public Officials Act and Article 34 of the Local Public Officials Remuneration Regulations, general fixed-term public officials at annual salary grade 4 or higher and those at Grade B or higher;
(c) Executives of public institutions falling under Article 2, subparagraph 3 (c) of the Official Information Disclosure Act and Article 2, subparagraph 2 of the Enforcement Decree of that Act.
(4) Among persons eligible for livelihood support payments under Article 9 (1) of the Act, a person who sustained an injury and did not receive compensation under Article 7 (1) 2 (b) of the Act shall be paid 4.8 million won per person. <Amended on October 31, 2007>
(5) Where a person simultaneously falls under more than one of the subparagraphs of Article 9 (1) of the Act, an amount favorable to the person eligible for payment may be selected and paid. <Amended on October 31, 2007>

Article 13 (Applications for Payment of Compensation, etc.)
(1) A person who intends to apply for payment of compensation, medical support payments, or livelihood support payments under Article 10 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "compensation, etc.") shall submit to the Committee, through the City/Do having jurisdiction over the applicant's address, an application for payment of compensation, etc. in attached Form 1 (a) through attached Form 1 (d) (including an application in electronic form), accompanied by the following documents (including electronic documents): <Amended on March 17, 2004; April 15, 2005; June 12, 2006; October 31, 2007; November 2, 2010>
1. Deleted. <June 12, 2006>
2. One copy of a certificate of matters recorded in the family relations register of the person concerned or a certified copy of a removed family register (limited to the bereaved family members of a deceased, missing, or injured person, where the matters cannot be verified by a certificate of matters recorded in the family relations register);
2-2. One copy of a statement of payment details for previously paid treatment expenses in attached Form 1-2 (c);
3. One copy of a form for selecting a representative of the bereaved family in attached Form 2 (limited to cases where a representative of the bereaved family has been selected);
4. One copy of a power of attorney for receipt of compensation, etc. in attached Form 3 (limited to cases where an application is made through a representative due to emigration, hospitalization, or other unavoidable circumstances);
5. One copy of a certificate of occupation and monthly salary in attached Form 4 (limited to persons earning employment income);
6. One copy of a certificate of occupation and monthly net earnings in attached Form 5 (limited to persons earning business income);
7. One copy of other evidentiary materials substantiating the grounds for the application.
(2) Where, in applying for and receiving compensation, etc. under paragraph (1), the bereaved family members of a deceased, missing, or injured person include two or more heirs to property of the same rank, a representative of the bereaved family shall be selected using the form for selecting a representative of the bereaved family in attached Form 2. Provided, That this shall not apply where an agreement among the heirs to property of the same rank is impossible.
(3) Where a person who intends to apply for payment of compensation, etc. under paragraph (1) is unable to apply for and receive compensation, etc. personally due to emigration, hospitalization, or other unavoidable circumstances, that person may appoint a representative by a power of attorney for receipt of compensation, etc. in attached Form 3, confirmed by one of the following persons:
1. The head of the overseas diplomatic mission, in cases of emigration or other residence abroad;
2. The head of the relevant medical institution, in cases of hospitalization;
3. The head of the relevant custodial institution, in cases of confinement in a prison, etc.;
4. The head of the Eup/Myeon/Dong, in other cases.
(4) Where the Committee receives an application for payment of compensation, etc. under paragraph (1) and the relevant documents under the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) are not attached, it shall require the applicant to supplement the application with those documents.
(5) The Committee receiving an application for payment of compensation, etc. under paragraph (1) shall verify a certified copy of the applicant's resident registration record through the joint use of administrative information under Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act. Provided, That where the applicant does not consent to verification, the Committee shall require the applicant to attach it. <Amended on November 2, 2010>

Article 14 (Applications for Restoration of Honor)
(1) A person who intends to apply for specific measures for restoration of honor under Article 5 (2) shall submit to the Committee, through the City/Do having jurisdiction over the applicant's address, an application for restoration of honor in attached Form 1 (e) (including an application in electronic form), together with the following documents (including electronic documents): <Amended on March 17, 2004; April 15, 2005; June 12, 2006; November 2, 2010>
1. Deleted. <June 12, 2006>
2. One copy of a certificate of matters recorded in the family relations register of the person concerned or a certified copy of a removed family register (limited to the bereaved family members of a deceased, missing, or injured person, where the matters cannot be verified by a certificate of matters recorded in the family relations register);
3. One copy of other evidentiary materials substantiating the grounds for the application.
(2) Article 13 (3) through (5) shall apply mutatis mutandis to the procedures for applications for restoration of honor under paragraph (1). <Amended on June 12, 2006>

Article 15 (Receipt of Applications and Investigation of Basic Facts)
(1) Applications under Articles 13 and 14 shall be received by the City/Do having jurisdiction over the applicant's domicile.
(2) In connection with an application received under paragraph (1), the mayor and the heads of the county and autonomous district having jurisdiction over the applicant's domicile may investigate the facts pursuant to Article 20 (1) of the Act.

Article 16 (Requests for Reexamination, etc.)
Where special grounds exist, the chairperson of the Committee may request the relevant subcommittee to reexamine or redetermine a matter examined or determined by that subcommittee under Article 7.

Article 17 (Decisions)
(1) A decision to pay compensation, etc. under Article 11 of the Act and a decision to restore honor under Article 5 of this Decree shall be based on reliable evidence.
(2) When the Committee makes a decision on compensation, a decision on the payment of livelihood support payments, or a decision on the restoration of honor, it shall prepare a written decision on compensation, a written decision on the payment of livelihood support payments, or a written decision on the restoration of honor in appended Form No. 6, and all members present at the meeting of the Committee shall affix their names and seals thereto. <Amended on April 15, 2005>

Article 18 (Notice)
(1) When the Committee makes a decision on compensation, a decision on the payment of livelihood support payments, or a decision on the restoration of honor, it shall retain the original of the written decision on compensation, written decision on the payment of livelihood support payments, or written decision on the restoration of honor, and shall serve on the applicant two authentic copies of the written decision and a notice of the decision on compensation, notice of the decision on the payment of livelihood support payments, or notice of the decision on the restoration of honor in appended Form No. 7. If the applicant has an agent, these documents shall be served on the agent, and one certified copy of the written decision on compensation, written decision on the payment of livelihood support payments, or written decision on the restoration of honor shall be served on the applicant. In such cases, the original of the written decision on compensation, written decision on the payment of livelihood support payments, or written decision on the restoration of honor may be retained as an electronic document or a digitized document under Article 5 of the Framework Act on Electronic Documents and Transactions. <Amended on November 12, 2024>
(2) The Committee shall notify the applicant of the details of measures taken under Articles 5-3 through 5-5 of the Act; if the applicant has an agent, it shall notify the agent thereof.

Article 19 (Application for Reconsideration)
A person who intends to apply for reconsideration under Article 13 of the Act shall submit to the Committee an application for reconsideration in appended Form No. 8, accompanied by the following documents:
1. One copy of a medical certificate of physical (mental) disability in appended Form No. 9 issued by a designated hospital, etc. (limited to cases in which an objection is raised to the determination of the disability grade);
2. One copy of other supporting materials that can substantiate the grounds for reconsideration.

Article 19-2 (Disclosure of Materials)
Where the applicant or a person authorized by the applicant requests disclosure of materials relating to the examination, the Committee may disclose the relevant materials pursuant to the Official Information Disclosure Act and the Personal Information Protection Act. <Amended on September 29, 2011>

Article 20 (Consent and Claim for Payment)
An applicant who has received a notice of a decision on compensation or a notice of a decision on the payment of livelihood support payments pursuant to the former part of Article 18 (1) shall, if the applicant wishes to receive compensation, etc., submit to the Committee a consent and claim form in appended Form No. 10, accompanied by the following documents: <Amended on November 12, 2024>
1. One authentic copy of the written decision on compensation or written decision on the payment of livelihood support payments;
2. One copy of the applicant's certificate of seal impression or certificate of personal signature confirmation;
3. One copy of the applicant's bankbook for the account into which the payment is to be deposited.

Article 21 (Paying Institution)
Compensation, etc. determined by the Committee shall be paid by the Committee; provided, the practical affairs thereof may be entrusted to the National Treasury (including agencies of the National Treasury).

Article 22 (Time of Payment)
Compensation, etc. shall be paid within 15 days from the date on which a claim for payment is made under Article 20.

Article 23 (Public Notice)
The chairperson of the Committee shall give public notice in the Official Gazette of the following matters concerning applications for compensation and the restoration of honor, and may also give public notice thereof in two or more daily newspapers, on an Internet website, through broadcasting, or by other means: <Amended on April 15, 2005; November 24, 2020>
1. Persons eligible;
2. Qualifications of applicants;
3. Institutions receiving applications;
4. Application period;
5. Required documents;
6. Criteria for calculating the amount payable;
7. Procedures for deliberation and decision;
8. Other matters necessary for applications and payment.

Article 24 (Applications for Project Expenses by Memorial Organizations, etc.)
Where a memorial organization, etc. intends to apply for project expenses, etc. pursuant to Article 24 (2) of the Act, it shall submit the following documents:
1. Articles of incorporation or rules of the organization;
2. A list of members;
3. Minutes of the regular general meeting for the relevant year (including the budget and statement of accounts);
4. A project plan.

Article 25 (Detailed Rules for Implementation)
Matters necessary for the implementation of this Decree shall be determined by the chairperson following a resolution of the Committee.

This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

ADDENDA (Decree Amending the Regulations on the Management of Parolees and Other Decrees for Electronic Processing of Civil Petitions) <No. 18312, March 17, 2004>

ADDENDA <No. 18792, April 15, 2005>

(1) (Enforcement Date) This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

(2) (Transitional Measures for Persons for Whom Payment of Compensation Has Been Decided) For persons for whom payment of compensation was decided before this Decree enters into force, compensation shall be adjusted and paid pursuant to the amended provisions of Article 11-2 as of the date this Decree enters into force; provided, compensation under Article 7 (1) 1 and 2 (b) of the Act shall be deducted.

(3) (Transitional Measures for Applicants for Livelihood Support Payments) A person who applied for the restoration of honor pursuant to Article 14 before this Decree enters into force shall be deemed to have applied for livelihood support payments. In such cases, a person who wishes to receive livelihood support payments shall submit to the Committee an application in appended Form No. 1 (e) and supporting documents.

ADDENDA (Decree Partially Amending the Enforcement Decree of the State Claims Management Act and Other Decrees for Joint Use of Administrative Information and Reduction of Documents) <No. 19507, June 12, 2006>

This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

ADDENDA (Regulations on Personnel Management of the Senior Executive Service) <No. 19513, June 12, 2006>

Article 4 (Amendments to Other Statutes and Regulations)
(1) through (93) Omitted.

(94) The Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Restoration of Honor of and Compensation to Persons Related to Democratization Movements is partially amended as follows:

In Article 6 (2), "Grade 2 or Grade 3 State public officials belonging to the Ministry of Government Administration and Home Affairs" shall be replaced with "Grade 3 public officials of the Ministry of Government Administration and Home Affairs or public officials in general service belonging to the Senior Executive Service".

In Article 12-2 (2) 2 (a), "public officials in general service of Grade 5 or higher" shall be replaced with "public officials in general service of Grade 5 or higher (including public officials in general service belonging to the Senior Executive Service)", and "Grade 5 or higher as the grade of intended appointment" shall be replaced with "Grade 5 or higher as the grade of intended appointment (including public officials in general service belonging to the Senior Executive Service)"; in item (b) of the same subparagraph, "public officials in special service equivalent to Grade 5 or higher" shall be replaced with "public officials in special service equivalent to Grade 5 or higher (including public officials in special service belonging to the Senior Executive Service)".

(95) through (241) Omitted.
